## 1. Introduction

This project examines how rising CO₂ emissions and changing patterns of renewable-energy adoption relate to global surface-temperature anomalies between 1990 and 2023. By integrating NASA’s global temperature records with country-level economic and environmental indicators, including CO₂ emissions, GDP per capita, population, and renewable-energy share, the study aims to uncover how human activities and energy choices shape global warming trends. The core motivation of this project is to quantify these relationships using data-driven methods, assess cross-country differences, and identify structural patterns such as emission clusters or fairness gaps. Through exploratory analysis, multivariate techniques, and predictive modeling, the project provides a comprehensive assessment of how emissions and socio-economic factors collectively influence climate outcomes, while highlighting the uneven burden climate change places on low-emitting nations.
